title: SSH Key-Based Login: Secure Remote Access

scenes.line1: How do you log in securely?
scenes.say: How do you log in to a Linux server securely? Why use SSH keys instead of passwords?

scenes.label: Keys
scenes.sub: Private key stays with you; public key goes on the server.
scenes.say: SSH uses a key pair. Your private key stays with you. The public key goes on the server.

scenes.title: Key-based login steps
scenes.say: Generate a key with ssh-keygen. Copy your public key to the server. Set strict permissions on your .ssh folder and authorized_keys file.
Permissions matter. .ssh should be 700, authorized_keys 600. Wrong permissions break key login without errors.

scenes.question: How do you block root SSH login?
scenes.say: If asked how to block root SSH login, don't just delete root's keys. Set PermitRootLogin to no in the SSH configuration.
